output.decision: Do not add another full tub of creatine: it directly conflicts with the observed cancellation reason of having too much product. Use a low-burden, non-consumable gift instead, preferably a simple shaker bottle (or let customers choose it versus no gift). The reminder should lead with shipment control—skip or delay—rather than urgency.
next_steps: Replace the proposed extra tub with a non-consumable accessory such as a shaker bottle; avoid adding more creatine inventory.

Send a pre-renewal reminder early enough for customers to change the order: “Your third creatine shipment is coming up. Have enough on hand? You can skip or delay your next delivery in a few clicks. If the timing works, we’ll include a complimentary shaker bottle as a thank-you.”
Make skip and delay actions prominent in the email/SMS and account flow; do not require support contact.
Test a gift-choice version against no gift to distinguish gift appeal from shipment-control impact.
Track skip, delay, cancellation, and repeat-order outcomes for third-shipment recipients.
missing_inputs: Current shipment cadence and how many days before renewal customers can edit orders.
Available accessory inventory, unit cost, and shipping/packaging impact.
Whether customers already receive a scoop, shaker, or comparable accessory.
Existing email/SMS consent, reminder timing, and skip/delay capabilities.
assumptions: General-knowledge recommendation; no library evidence was supplied.
The stated “too much product” cancellation reason is sufficiently material to avoid gifting additional creatine.
A shaker bottle is compatible with the brand and can be fulfilled without creating a meaningful packaging or cost issue.
